title: Read the batch time off the concrete ticket before it's poured
why: A truck stuck in traffic arrives with concrete that was mixed nearly two hours ago, and it goes into the slab because nobody did the sum. If it fails its cube tests later, there is no record of when it should have been refused.
idea: Photograph every delivery ticket as the truck arrives. The iPhone can copy the printed batch time straight off the photo, and a small sheet works out how long ago the concrete was mixed and goes red if it's over your spec's limit, before the chute swings round.
how: Photograph the delivery ticket at the gate, before discharge.
Touch and hold the batch time in the photo (iPhone's Live Text) and copy it.
Paste it into the pour log on the phone; the sheet subtracts it from the current time.
Over the limit in your concrete specification, the row turns red and the load is checked before it goes in.
need: The time limit from your concrete specification (check yours; don't assume)
A simple pour log in Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets on the phone
Someone at the gate with the authority to hold a truck
before:
Ticket: Truck 14, batched 07:52, 8 m³ C30/37
Arrived: 09:31
after:
Truck 14: 99 minutes since batching → RED, check before discharge
Logged with photo and time, for the quality records
person: A person decides whether to accept, test or refuse the load. The sheet only does the arithmetic and keeps the record.
watch_out: Faded or crumpled tickets can't be read by the phone: type the time in by hand.
Make sure the phone clock and the plant's clock agree, or the minutes are wrong.
Time is only one test: admixtures and the temperature change what is acceptable.
explain: We photograph each concrete ticket at the gate and the phone tells us how old the load is, so late loads are caught before they're in the slab.
image_prompt: a concrete mixer truck at a site gate, a worker photographing a delivery ticket with a phone
credit: Written by hand for this column.
